verdictBasis: The operative content is right, including the claim that carries the most weight in this whole family — that condition 1's standing becomes MET for architecture-preview scope. I tested that against D-001's actual text and it holds. The single SHOULD-FIX is one sentence in the Readiness effect that mischaracterises another condition's standing, and that sentence lands verbatim in the permanent register.

shouldFixRecorded.location: Readiness effect — 'Conditions 2–5 remain NOT MET / PARTLY MET.'
shouldFixRecorded.finding: Condition 3 is MET. file 08's readiness table reads '| 3 | DR-201–205 each `ACCEPTED` | **5 of 5 `ACCEPTED`** | **MET** |'. The live standings across the range are: condition 2 NOT MET, condition 3 MET, condition 4 PARTLY MET, condition 5 NOT MET. The sentence asserts that each of 2 through 5 is NOT MET or PARTLY MET, and one of the four is neither.
shouldFixRecorded.whyItMatters: Adopted entries carry their Readiness effect line into COORD verbatim — I checked D-070, D-081 and D-083 and all three do — so this is not working text but a statement destined for the permanent register. It also sits in the readiness statement of the one entry in this family that changes a readiness condition's standing, which is where a reader will look to understand what did and did not move.
shouldFixRecorded.departureFromTheFamilyForm: No earlier entry attempted this characterisation. Every prior instance uses the safe formulation — 'Conditions 2–5 remain' or 'Conditions 2–5 remain independently required' — which asserts continuity without asserting standings. D-084 is the first to state the standings, and states one of them wrongly.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: It changes nothing the entry does. Clause 4's replacement text for the condition-1 row is accurate and self-contained, clause 6 confines the edit and states 'Does not edit the nine existing D-070/D-081 notes', and no proposed file-08 text contains this sentence. The error is confined to the entry's own readiness statement.
shouldFixRecorded.fix: Either revert to the family form — 'Conditions 2–5 remain' — or state the standings accurately: condition 2 NOT MET, condition 3 MET, condition 4 PARTLY MET, condition 5 NOT MET.

summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. This entry flips condition 1's standing, so I tested that claim hardest rather than the mechanics. It holds: D-001's checklist reads 'DR-001 through DR-011 are SATISFIED or the owning V1 authority records an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition that names what may be designed without pretending the blocked semantics are settled', and with DR-001 SATISFIED and DR-002 through DR-011 all owner-recorded the qualifying set is 11 of 11. The entry scopes the claim to preview only, states 'Condition 1 is not SATISFIED of any residual', and keeps DR-011 HARD-BLOCKED with residuals not CLOSED. The preamble count moves nine to ten — the embedded count I failed to check one cycle ago — and its quoted Current text is verbatim in the register. My objection is one sentence in the Readiness effect that says conditions 2 through 5 are NOT MET or PARTLY MET when condition 3 is MET, and that sentence goes into COORD as written.
objections: C2-D084-SF1 — Readiness effect mischaracterises condition 3, which is MET, as NOT MET / PARTLY MET.
whatIVerified: Prompt digest at start and end: 30cc8b9d4c1d217e2dac5f9de4b776dde6f83366175d0a48b5abc36714a425c2, equal to the dispatch-supplied value. Subject at 7600f5800491fc832ce2949d0cb2cd582f4b1462d85d8a0bc5cf62f0f6379ed5, equal to both. Three measurements each at start and again at end; both -r--r--r-- at both ends.

The condition-1 MET claim is legitimate under D-001's own text, which I read rather than assumed. The checklist limb is 'DR-001 through DR-011 are SATISFIED or the owning V1 authority records an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition that names what may be designed without pretending the blocked semantics are settled.' DR-001 is SATISFIED and DR-002 through DR-011 each have an owner-recorded preview disposition, so the qualifying set is 11 of 11. I checked the one element that could have failed after v3's repair — whether a disposition that adds no independent semantic permission still 'names what may be designed'. It does: P-011-A names the permitted set by reference to nine pinned dispositions plus D-002 / D-018, and adds none. Naming by reference is still naming.

The claim is scoped rather than absolute, in four places: clause 4's text says 'MET for architecture-preview scope only (qualifying set = 11)' and adds 'Condition 1 is not SATISFIED of any residual'; the same text states 'DR-011 residuals R01–R16 remain not CLOSED'; clause 1 keeps DR-011 HARD-BLOCKED; and the readiness effect repeats 'Zero SATISFIED added. Residuals stay not CLOSED.'

The attack 'leaves preamble count at nine' fails. Clause 2 replaces 'one SATISFIED and nine explicitly disposed' with 'one SATISFIED and ten explicitly disposed', and I verified the quoted Current text is verbatim in live file 08 and that the ten version is not yet present. I checked this first because it is the exact defect I missed on D-081, where I confirmed the two-axis sentence existed without reading to the end of it where the count sits.

The attack 'counts residuals as CLOSED' fails, and the arithmetic reflects it. The new row reads '1 of 11 SATISFIED; 10 of 11 explicitly disposed', with 'Arithmetic: 1 + 10 + 0 = 11' — the zero being unresolved rows, not closed residuals — followed immediately by 'DR-011 residuals R01–R16 remain not CLOSED'. Clause 1 states 'Residuals stay not CLOSED' and clause 6 'Does not close any residual'. The alternatives reject promoting DR-011's lead label on the ground that 'residuals remain not CLOSED; DR-204'.

The ten named rows in the new condition-1 row are correct and complete: DR-001 SATISFIED, then DR-002 (D-058), DR-003 (D-065), DR-004 (D-064), DR-005 (D-060 + RB-DR005-V2-A1), DR-006 (D-077), DR-007 (D-078), DR-008 integration half (D-061), DR-009 (D-079 + RB-DR009-V2-A1), DR-010 (D-068), DR-011 parent (D-083 + RB-DR011-V3-A1/A2/A3). Both existing riders and all three new ones are carried into the register text rather than flattened.

The attack 'new file-08 status token' fails: the header states 'Does not coin a new file-08 status token', clause 1 keeps leading labels as the sole status-token source with DR-011 at HARD-BLOCKED, and clause 3 declines to change the snapshot heading date.

Appending is correct rather than duplicating: file 08 currently contains nine preview-scope owner-recording notes and DR-011 carries none, so this adds the tenth. Clause 6's 'Does not edit the nine existing D-070/D-081 notes' matches that count exactly.

The DR-011 note's remaining-work text reproduces the v3 disposition's whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA in full — all three items, the third lowercased for mid-sentence flow but otherwise identical — and the note pins the disposition digest f1c7f6b7… plus all three operative riders.

All five cited digests match live bytes: COORD 5aaadb89…, file 08 1360a4f8…, the freeze e809d439…, claim-register.v1 767dc210…, and the v3 disposition f1c7f6b7…. Both commits resolve: 8c9e8104 'D-083: owner-record DR-011 preview parent disposition' and b1885620 'D-081: file-08 notes for DR-006/007/009 owner recordings'.

The attacks 'freeze or claim-register motion' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fail: clause 6 states 'Does not apply a V1 successor. Does not move the freeze or claim register. Does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/', the header repeats the last, and the readiness effect ends 'Condition 5 remains last'. Pinning the freeze and claim register is apt given that promise.

The cycle framing is accurate: 'Not a fourth turn of D-070 or D-081', 'This entry does not overturn D-081. It uses the same two-axis algorithm and adds one more scoped note', and the alternatives reject freezing the D-081 count with a citation to ADV-D081-01 — the finding that produced that count.

Reversibility is scoped to exactly what changes: 'C-D084 plus restore of the prior DR-011 cell, prior condition-1 row, and prior preamble count ("nine"). Does not overturn D-081 or D-083.' Three limbs for three changes.
file 08 is unedited and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture, so this reviews the authorization rather than a performed edit. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

Whether conditions 2, 4 and 5 are correctly standing at NOT MET, PARTLY MET and NOT MET on their own merits. I read their current standings from file 08's readiness table to test the entry's characterisation; I did not audit whether those standings are themselves right.

Whether condition 1's substantive readiness is genuine beyond the checklist limb being satisfied. D-001's item 1 is a documentary test — SATISFIED or a scoped reviewed disposition — and eleven of eleven now meet it. Whether the underlying V1 work is actually done is a different question the entry does not claim and I did not assess.
The merits of the ten owner recordings and their dispositions, beyond my separate reviews of those I saw, whose stated limits I carry forward.
The sixteen DR-011 residuals. This entry leaves every one not CLOSED; I confirmed that claim is repeated three times but did not re-audit their statuses this cycle.
Whether the performed edit, once made, matches this authorization. The pins make that check possible afterwards.

objectNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX, and the shape matters because this entry is doing something none of its predecessors did. It moves a readiness condition from NOT MET to MET, and that claim is sound: I read D-001's item 1 rather than relying on the entry's summary, confirmed that a zero-new-permission parent disposition still names what may be designed, and confirmed the scoping to preview only alongside the explicit 'Condition 1 is not SATISFIED of any residual'. The preamble count moves nine to ten with a verbatim Current quote, which is the check I failed to make one cycle ago and made first this time. What I cannot pass is a sentence beside all that saying conditions 2 through 5 are NOT MET or PARTLY MET when condition 3 has been MET at 5 of 5 ACCEPTED. Every earlier entry wrote 'Conditions 2–5 remain' and asserted nothing about standings; this one asserts, gets one wrong, and the Readiness effect line goes into COORD verbatim.
